sections.name: architecture
sections.value: The shared DDL boundary is crates/store/src/admin.rs: create_database, drop_database, and drop_database_if_idle take one process-wide tokio semaphore sized from FS3_DB_MUTATION_CONCURRENCY (default 1, max 2), so testkit, store integration support, doctor, and sandbox callers using the API cannot bypass it. FreshDatabase delegates without a second permit. Its create panic distinguishes no listener, authentication/permission rejection, and connected-then-closed/recovery. Orphan listing parses both minted shapes, selects only pg_stat_database rows with numbackends=0, and each sweep drop rechecks liveness under the permit and uses unforced DROP to fail safe on a race. crates/testkit/examples/list_orphans.rs is the read-only production listing seam.

value.rationale: One unit, one coder, no PM; o-prime coordinates directly (Jordan GO on row 126, 2026-09-02).

value.name: fresh-db-serialise
value.paths: crates/store/src/admin.rs, crates/store/tests/support/mod.rs, crates/store/Cargo.toml, crates/testkit/src/fresh_database.rs, crates/testkit/src/lib.rs, crates/testkit/examples/list_orphans.rs, and their tests
value.responsibility: fs3_store serialises every API-mediated CREATE/DROP process-wide; FreshDatabase advice is truthful across absent, auth, and recovery cases; orphan listing and sweep match minted names while preserving active databases.
value.interface: FreshDatabase existing signatures remain; FS3_DB_MUTATION_CONCURRENCY controls store-level DDL concurrency (default 1, max 2); list_orphans_from returns idle candidates; list_orphans example prints them read-only; fs3_store adds idle_database_names_with_prefix and drop_database_if_idle.
value.test_strategy: N=8 real create_database calls with an in-flight counter, red when the create-path permit is removed; advice tests for refused port, bad password, and listening-close; sweep test with two idle old names, one live old name, and one fresh name, red without numbackends filter plus a no-hang timeout; listing example before/after count; real store-suite and oversize checkpoint/log windows.
value.note: ac-0001–0004 by test/real usage in the worktree; ac-0005 with o-prime on the prod server.

Worktree-per-coder on the plan branch and follow-up branch, with a per-seat CARGO_TARGET_DIR. All test DDL targets the dedicated flowspace3-db-test postmaster through FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL on :5434, with small scratch-name sets and one cargo invocation at a time. NEVER :5433 or :7373. Production orphan listing/drop is o-prime-owned. Use absolute paths; rs delivery is by files under .harness/temp/agent plus short pij sends.

value.steps: None — single unit. o-prime squash-merges; no bounce needed (testkit only, no daemon binary change).
value.integration_proof: ac-0004 (oversize suite at default parallelism, postgres log clean) and ac-0005 (prod-server orphan listing then sweep on GO), both real usage.

value.when: spawned by o-prime once the PR is up
value.inputs: Plan, impl-guide, backpressure, committed review record, and PR receipts. Reviewer delta 09509b7 independently measured the 16 -> 2 -> 1 DDL trajectory and mutation-proved the restored runtime and no-FORCE guards; its verdict is APPROVE. Follow-up review covers only f-1a1a seed-age plausibility and f-1a10 hook construction unless behavior changes beyond them. Known-open product rows remain 110 and 122; the dedicated test postmaster is landed.

value.text: A process-wide static Semaphore across multiple tokio runtimes (each #[tokio::test] builds its own) — a tokio Semaphore in a static is runtime-agnostic, but verify; std::sync::Mutex held across .await is the trap
Serialising creates slows suites that mint many DBs — measure the oversize suite before/after and report; N knob exists for that reason
The sweep parser matching too broadly and dropping a non-test database — the shape requires `<epoch>_<32hex>` tail; assert prod-like names (flowspace3, flowspace3_test) are never candidates
